Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ott

Class OttFactors

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.ott.OttFactors
@Configuration(proxyBeanMethods=false) public class OttFactors extends Object
Registers the one-time token methods as authentication factors. One authority cannot carry two strengths and the registry refuses two factors with the same authority, so each use of each channel is a factor of its own: the e-mail code or magic link as a sign-in (FACTOR_OTT, Spring Security's own constant) and the SMS code as a sign-in are FactorStrength.PRIMARY (they prove the possession of a mailbox or a phone, which is as strong as a password and no more), and the same two as the second factor of a user who already signed in with a primary factor are FactorStrength.SECOND. The amr values are those of RFC 8176: otp for the code or the link sent by e-mail and sms for the code sent by SMS.
